prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-13. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 2.29 |
| Retained earnings       | 1,385M |
| Current liabilities     | 6,019M |
| Current assets          | 13,790M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 18,899M |
| Total liabilities       | 27,401M |
| Total assets            | 58,167M |
| EBIT / operating income | 811M |
| Revenue                 | 5,633M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-13, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided metrics indicate moderate leverage (total liabilities/assets of ~47%, liabilities/equity of ~1.45) with solid liquidity (current ratio of 2.29). However, profitability is weak (EBIT margin of ~14% but implied ROA of only ~1.4% and ROE of ~4%), and retained earnings are low relative to the balance sheet, pointing to limited financial flexibility and an overall profile consistent with the lower end of investment-grade.
DECISION: BBB
(The rating is assigned purely from the static ratios above; no forward-looking adjustments or peer comparisons are possible without additional data such as interest coverage or cash-flow volatility.)
